bib.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv v2, 24 May 2019; Google AI Language)

question: Can pre-training deep bidirectional Transformer representations with a masked-LM objective, then fine-tuning with one added output layer, beat unidirectional pre-training and task-specific architectures across many NLP tasks?
hypothesis: A deep bidirectional model is strictly more powerful than a left-to-right model or a shallow concatenation of left-to-right and right-to-left models, and scaling the pre-trained model helps even small downstream tasks.
contributions: Demonstrate the importance of bidirectional pre-training for language representations (masked LMs, vs unidirectional LMs of Radford 2018 and shallow concatenation of Peters 2018a).

Show pre-trained representations reduce the need for heavily-engineered task-specific architectures; first fine-tuning-based representation model with SOTA on a large suite of sentence-level and token-level tasks.
Advance the state of the art for eleven NLP tasks; code and pre-trained models released.

method.summary: Multi-layer bidirectional Transformer encoder pre-trained on BooksCorpus + English Wikipedia with masked LM (15% of WordPiece tokens) and next sentence prediction, then fine-tuned end-to-end per task with one added output layer. Two sizes: BASE (110M) and LARGE (340M).
method.task: Pre-training (MLM + NSP) then fine-tuning on GLUE, SQuAD v1.1/v2.0, SWAG; feature-based NER on CoNLL-2003

datasets.name: English Wikipedia
datasets.preprocessing: only text passages extracted; lists, tables and headers ignored; document-level corpus used to get long contiguous sequences

datasets.name: GLUE (MNLI, QQP, QNLI, SST-2, CoLA, STS-B, MRPC, RTE; WNLI excluded)
datasets.size: train examples: MNLI 392k, QQP 363k, QNLI 108k, SST-2 67k, CoLA 8.5k, STS-B 5.7k, MRPC 3.5k, RTE 2.5k
datasets.split: Test scored by GLUE evaluation server (single submission per model); hyperparameters chosen on Dev
datasets.preprocessing: WNLI excluded; majority class predicted for GLUE submission

datasets.name: TriviaQA (augmentation for SQuAD v1.1)
datasets.preprocessing: paragraphs from TriviaQA-Wiki formed of the first 400 tokens in documents that contain at least one provided possible answer; fine-tune on TriviaQA before SQuAD

datasets.name: CoNLL-2003 NER
datasets.source: Tjong Kim Sang and De Meulder 2003
datasets.preprocessing: case-preserving WordPiece, maximal document context, first sub-token used for tagging, no CRF

models.name: BERT-BASE
models.architecture: bidirectional Transformer encoder (Vaswani 2017, tensor2tensor); gelu activation

models.name: ELMo (BiLSTM+ELMo+Attn)
models.architecture: concatenated independent left-to-right and right-to-left LSTMs, feature-based

training.objective: Sum of mean masked-LM likelihood and mean next-sentence-prediction likelihood. MLM: 15% of WordPiece token positions chosen; of those 80% [MASK], 10% random token, 10% unchanged; cross entropy on original token. NSP: 50% B is the true next segment (IsNext), 50% random (NotNext), predicted from [CLS].
training.epochs: approximately 40 epochs over the 3.3 billion word corpus
training.tokens: inferred: 1M steps * 128,000 tokens/batch = 128B tokens (the paper gives 128,000 tokens/batch and 1M steps)
training.seq_len: combined length <=512 tokens; sequence length 128 for 90% of steps, 512 for last 10%
training.hardware: BERT-BASE: 4 Cloud TPUs in Pod configuration (16 TPU chips); BERT-LARGE: 16 Cloud TPUs (64 TPU chips)

other.finetune_general: batch size 16 or 32; Adam lr 5e-5/3e-5/2e-5; epochs 2/3/4; dropout 0.1; pick best on Dev
other.finetune_GLUE: batch 32, 3 epochs, lr chosen from 5e-5,4e-5,3e-5,2e-5 on Dev; BERT-LARGE: several random restarts (same checkpoint, different shuffling and classifier init), best on Dev; single test submission each
other.finetune_SQuAD1.1: 3 epochs, lr 5e-5, batch 32; new start and end vectors S,E in R^H
other.finetune_SQuAD2.0: 2 epochs, lr 5e-5, batch 48; no-answer = span at [CLS]; predict non-null if s_hat > s_null + tau, tau tuned on dev for F1
other.finetune_SWAG: 3 epochs, lr 2e-5, batch 16; four sequences, one score vector dotted with C
other.finetune_cost: all results replicable in at most 1 hour on a single Cloud TPU or a few hours on a GPU from the same pre-trained model; SQuAD model in about 30 minutes on a single Cloud TPU (Dev F1 91.0%)
other.NER_feature_based: activations from BERT-BASE fed to randomly initialised two-layer 768-dim BiLSTM; NER results averaged over 5 random restarts
other.model_size_ablation: Table 6 reports average Dev accuracy over 5 random restarts of fine-tuning

inference.decoding: SQuAD: maximum scoring span with j>=i, score S.Ti + E.Tj
inference.samples: SQuAD v1.1 ensemble is 7x systems with different pre-training checkpoints and fine-tuning seeds; NER averaged over 5 restarts

metrics.name: GLUE Test score
metrics.definition: accuracy for most tasks, F1 for QQP and MRPC, Spearman for STS-B; Average excludes WNLI so differs from official GLUE score

metrics.name: SQuAD EM / F1
metrics.definition: exact match and token-overlap F1 of predicted span

metrics.name: SWAG accuracy
metrics.definition: choose most plausible of four continuations

metrics.name: MLM held-out perplexity
metrics.definition: masked LM perplexity of held-out training data

baselines: SQuAD leaderboard systems (nlnet, QANet, BiDAF+ELMo, R.M. Reader)
eval.protocol: Single-task fine-tuning; hyperparameters picked on Dev; GLUE Test via single server submission per model; entries using BERT as a component excluded from comparisons.

availability.data: BooksCorpus and Wikipedia (public); exact Wikipedia snapshot not stated

limits: Only English; no multitask fine-tuning (footnote 14 notes it could help, e.g. RTE).
Pre-train/fine-tune mismatch from [MASK] mitigated by 80/10/10 but not eliminated; MLM converges slightly slower than LTR (App C.1).
Several differences from GPT beyond bidirectionality (data size, batch size, [CLS]/[SEP] at pre-training, per-task lr); ablation uses BERT-BASE-size models only.
BERT-LARGE fine-tuning unstable on small datasets; best of several restarts chosen on Dev.
SQuAD leaderboard comparisons are dated Dec 10th, 2018 and leaderboard systems lacked public descriptions.
Seeds, precision and total FLOPs not given; Wikipedia snapshot not stated.

terms.definition: randomly mask some percentage of input tokens and predict the masked tokens; final hidden vectors at mask positions go to a softmax over the vocabulary
binarized task: 50% of the time B is the actual next sentence (IsNext), 50% a random sentence (NotNext)
